facts.value: pre-registered decision tree for what to do after the six points are fit (docs/lessons/scaling_decision_tree.md v1.8, frozen before the points run): three mechanical reads -- doubling gain d_double=(L(Dmax)-E)(1-2^-beta), asymptote gap R=L(Dmax)-E, recognition levels (math twin / minimal pairs / LAMBADA at Dmax) -- drive the branches: d_double>=0.05 and R>0.10 -> extend D; R<0.05 -> data scaling done, read recognition: twin>0.75 + pairs>0.75 + LAMBADA>0.30 + generative<0.02 = recognition ceiling (knowledge present, production absent) -> SFT first, scale N only if SFT fails to move generation; twin<0.60 or pairs<0.60 = knowledge absent -> change data recipe. v1.1 adds the reweight branch (section 2a): triggered when E2 per-domain slope spread max-min > 2xSE and the flattest-slope domain's weight >=10% (web_hq: -0.123 vs textbook/en -0.26, weight 32.4%); anti-trigger = offsets differ but slopes equal (offset is intrinsic entropy, not waste -- never reweight on offsets alone); when d_double<0.05 reweight is the only live data-side action, when >=0.05 reweight goes first (zero new corpus, one mix json) and its result calibrates whether E2 slopes predict reallocation gains. Reweight read pre-registered: same-D old/new mix checkpoints, aggregate val NLL improvement >0.05 = lever holds, <=0.05 = lever retired. Shift capped at 10pt of weight (linearity untested beyond). Identification limit: E2 domains co-varied across the ladder, slopes are ranked observations not causal marginals -- the reweight run IS the experiment. Fixed-N optimum: D* = smallest D with L(D)<=E+0.05 (within noise of the asymptote); the curve values only the 'more data' option, the tree puts alternatives on the same ruler. Fit-failure branches pre-registered (U-shape -> regime boundary, monotone drift -> wrong form, RMS>0.10 -> panel-only decision). Thresholds anchored to run-to-run noise (0.05, Kaplan) and the known-answer calibrations v1.2 adds section 3d (architecture migration of the recognition thresholds, written before the points run): the 0.75/0.75/0.30/0.02 thresholds are absolute claims (twin 0.75 = 3:1 discrimination), old-arch measurements were only feasibility evidence; after the six points, before reading the Dmax branch, re-run known-answer on the new arch's strongest checkpoint -- spread <60pt cuts the metric, reading below the absolute threshold lowers it by the fraction-of-demonstrated-range rule (two-way: 0.5+0.557*(ceiling-0.5), 0.557=(0.75-0.5)/(0.949-0.5); LAMBADA: 0.843*ceiling, 0.843=0.30/0.356; pass@1 stays absolute 0.02), recalibrated numbers frozen before the branch read, weakening reported. Section 6 table now labels every threshold measured/chosen with its source; the four 0.05s declared the same deliberate 1x-noise reuse v1.3 adds the corpus-quality interpretation clause (section 4 supplement, written before the points run): web_hq skipped the top-40% quality-head cut this version, so the six points train on a dirtier corpus than declared. Rules frozen: E is 'this corpus's floor', not 'the model's ceiling' -- no external comparison (Chinchilla 1.69 etc.); R=L(Dmax)-E is immune to ADDITIVE entropy (both terms shift, R unchanged), the misfire risk is only the non-additive case (noise tokens bend the curve flat at smaller D, capacity saturated on noise), unmeasurable until 44's W/F; R<0.05 reads as 'scaling done ON THIS CORPUS'; if section 3b (recognition absent) triggers, dirty corpus is a known suspect and the quality cut is the first recipe-change candidate; beta is immune to a constant noise fraction (D'=c*D absorbed by B only, beta unchanged) -- the warmup overestimate remains the only known beta bias. W/F is the pre-registered falsifier: E_W < E_dirty-0.05 -> floor was inflated, tree re-walked on W curve; R_W>0.10 where R_dirty<0.05 -> non-additive flattening confirmed, extend-D reopens on clean corpus; both within 0.05 -> the cut is worth ~0 at this scale. fb's intuition that 'R is compressed by entropy' was refined in the clause: additive entropy cancels in R. v1.6 flags the steep pole as single-source: textbook/en (both -0.26) share the source chinese-cosmopedia (en domain is 85% Chinese, cause traced to build_domains.sh:32 merging cosmopedia_extra.jsonl + en_textbook.jsonl, container label read as language label) -- the slope spread's steep end is one source counted twice, not two independent witnesses; trigger reading unchanged, reweight direction argument narrowed to 'web_hq -> cosmopedia'. v1.7: section 5 RMS>0.10 aligned to 2.28*sigma-hat = 0.1176 (was 2.3x Kaplan sigma; the 0.10-0.1176 band would have contradicted the protocol). v1.8 (expressive-ability ladder read, frozen before 3.24b lands): GAP = L2-O1 (74pt at 0.2b: two-way 90.4% vs open acc@1 16.0%) is the steering quantity for the user's 表达能力 target; O1 is not in the SKIP class (old-arch 3.24b held-out 35.6% demonstrates headroom, acc@5/acc@1 = 2.3x internal structure, seed noise s_O1=1.02pt df=3 << 74pt gap); noise floor self-calibrated from the 4 seeds (be.panel_expressive_seed_variance: s_L2=0.54, s_O1=1.02, s_O5=1.47, s_CE=1.27, s_GAP=0.90pt; readable move >= 4.65*s_M -> L2 2.5/O1 4.8/O5 6.8/CE 5.9/GAP 4.2pt); four shapes pre-registered -- A volume (O1 moves, gap narrows -> composition hypothesis weakened), B composition (L2/CE move, O1 flat -> hypothesis survives, 10x needs composition change), C both-move, D unreadable; mechanism premise measured: cosmopedia template concentration 6.38x web_hq (44, mlm.corpus.cosmopedia_template_concentration), necessity holds, consequence is the ladder's; the ladder can FALSIFY the composition hypothesis but not confirm it (flat at 3.24b does not prove flat at 36B); RETRACTED 2026-09-02, same day, by the fix its own uncertainty asked for. The defect described below was real on the code that produced the p500m checkpoints, and is gone from main: 52aec31 adds `+ int(_base.get(n, 0))` at train.py:1030, where _base is the cursor build_mix APPLIED (train.py:1580), so a post-resume save writes an ABSOLUTE row count instead of a segment count. VERIFIED on three real checkpoints of the current run, read on the pod with the equality the uncertainty named -- sum(row_cursor) == row_cursor_as_of_step x batch x accum x world, rows/step = 16x2x8 = 256: step500 128,000 = 500x256; interrupt.step832 212,992 = 832x256; interrupt.step1192 305,152 = 1192x256. Only the third has discriminating power -- it was written after a resume at origin 832, where absolute and segment-only disagree (305,152 against 92,160), and 305,152 - 212,992 = 92,160 = 360x256 is exactly the 360 steps of that segment added in. The first two sit at origin 0, where both implementations give the same number and the old code would also read green. THE COST OF LEAVING THIS AT status=measured: on 2026-09-02 the controller session chose to resume the 200M run from step832 rather than step1192 to avoid the re-read this entry predicts, discarding 360 steps = 1.36 card-hours against a risk that no longer existed. A fact whose code has been fixed is not merely stale; it is acted on. WHAT SURVIVES: the p500m numbers below are a correct reading of the old behaviour, and eff.resume_inflates_total_steps cites its 8,192-row overlap for that run. WHAT DOES NOT: any prediction about a resume on current main.

The row cursor counts ONE SEGMENT and does not accumulate, so the SECOND and every later resume re-reads rows the run has already trained on. train.py:1387 computes rows_done = (step - _origin) * batch * accum, and :2309 sets _origin = resume_step, so a checkpoint written after a resume describes only the rows THAT resume drew -- not the run's total. Measured on p500m_20b_0902 (de and tilerl, independently, same hour): the nine domain cursors in .interrupt.step32 sum to 8,192 = 32x256, correct because that segment started at origin 0; the cursors in .interrupt.step83 sum to 13,056 = 51x256, while step 83 had truly consumed 21,248 = 83x256. Neither checkpoint records the total, and nothing raises. Relaunching from .interrupt.step83 seeded used[] with 13,056 against FULL pools, so rows 13,056..21,248 were read a SECOND time: 8,192 rows, 33.5M tokens, 0.168% of the 20B budget. Those rows are at epoch 2.0 while the corpus around them is at 1.0. Nine srcfp fingerprints matched and no domain reset to row 0, so de-13's discard fix is confirmed working in production by the same artifact.

config.how_it_happened: segment 1 fresh -> SIGTERM at 32; segment 2 --resume step32 -> SIGTERM at 83; segment 3 --resume step83, hand-written, is the second resume. supervise_run.sh allows exactly one automatic resume for this reason; the second was a human relaunch, which is how the cost came to be measured rather than assumed.

From the second resume on, the rows re-read equal the length of the FIRST segment, whatever that was. Here: 8,192 rows = 33.5M tokens = 0.168%. The quantity does not grow with later resumes; it is re-paid once per resume beyond the first. AS OF 52aec31 the boundary is moot on main: no resume re-reads a segment, because the count written is absolute. The boundary still describes any checkpoint written before 52aec31 (2026-09-02 18:10 +0800), which includes every p500m_20b_0902 interrupt file.

That is enough to kill the claim -- the claim predicted 92,160 and the file says 305,152 -- but it does not establish that the absolute count is right for every shape: all three files come from one run at one (batch, accum, world), and a checkpoint saved mid-accumulation or with a domain whose cursor was DISCARDED (corpus fp change, seed change) is untested. The discard path is the one to watch: train.py:1580 sets _base only in the branch that applied the cursor, so a discarded domain contributes 0 to _base by design, and the equality would then fail legitimately -- the assert must not fire there. beta_drifts_with_window.precedent: pretrain_15b_s1 drifted 0.6486 (first 4) to 0.4187 (all 32), -0.23, converging only near step 16000 (b0)

config.triple_spread_is_a_range: The five triples recorded earlier still span exactly 0.8308; each triple's beta uses only its own three points and does not move when the run produces more. The 1.1914 spread is over NINE triples -- it grew because four triples were ADDED, not because the curve degraded. A sample range only ever grows with sample size, so 'more points gave a wider spread' is not evidence about the data. The claim that survives is the least-squares drift, which is computed on a fixed estimator over a growing window and is monotone.

(2000,4000,6000).why: margin below 0.2, where beta's relative error reaches the 30% scale; this close to the no-solution boundary the value is not a number

fixed_estimator_sliding_window.estimator: geometric k=2, (d, 2d, 4d), the SAME shape at three different starts -- not a change of estimator
fixed_estimator_sliding_window.reading: The three span 0.3028 while each carries a quantisation bound of 0.014-0.025: they disagree by 12 to 22 times their own uncertainty, and all three margins clear the 0.2 usability floor. THE EVIDENCE IS THE DISAGREEMENT, NOT A TREND. A true single-parameter power law returns the same beta from every window within noise; no direction or monotonicity needs to be claimed, and with n=3 none could be. b0 offered this as a weak trend claim; it is a strong consistency failure.

facts.uncertainty: THE DOMINANT TERM IS ESTIMATOR CHOICE. Nine three-point triples on this curve give beta from 0.1146 to 1.3060. Beyond that, the least-squares value itself is NOT STATIONARY: it fell monotonically 0.7694 -> 0.6262 -> 0.6215 -> 0.5909 as the window grew from 4 to 12 points, -0.18 cumulative, reproducing the direction measured on pretrain_15b_s1 (-0.23 over 32 points, converging only near step 16000). A single number with an error bar is the wrong shape for this quantity in this window. Never quote it with a rounding-derived bound.
facts.boundary: CLOSED 2026-09-03 at step 6000 by fb+b0: the finding is that this curve does not follow a single-parameter power law over the observed window, and more points make the fit's beta move rather than settle. Evidence: three windows of ONE fixed estimator (geometric k=2) returning 0.7558 / 0.4530 / 0.5204, disagreeing by 12-22x their own quantisation bounds -- a consistency failure that needs no trend; monotone least-squares drift -0.18 over a growing window, max|residual| 20.1x print precision, and the pretrain_15b_s1 precedent. NOT evidence: the widening three-point range, which widened because triples were added. The sign test reads as noise (longest run 3, 5 changes against 5.5 expected) and that only rules out a systematic one-way deviation. beta does NOT enter the params-vs-data comparison, which reads two equal-FLOPs legs off their final domain loss; the step-13500 triple is cancelled because it would add one more three-point estimate to a spread already spanning 1.19.
